newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BAYERN DISPUTES BAD FOR BUNDESLIGA, SAYS SAMMER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAYERN DISPUTES BAD FOR BUNDESLIGA, SAYS SAMMER.

text.p: Borussia Dortmund's international Matthias Sammer has stepped into the squabbles which are threatening Bayern Munich's German title bid.
Despite their position at the top, Bayern are still struggling with the kind of internal battles which have persuaded Germany captain Juergen Klinsmann to quit the club.
Their build-up to Saturday's game at Hamburg has been dominated by more controversy involving Klinsmann and midfielder Mario Basler.

Sammer said Bayern's battles were bad for the German game. "We are all suffering because of it. This drama is ruining the credibility of our football," Sammer said. "Nobody has any respect for anybody else. Everyone is having a go at the others.
"It's not about the subject in hand anymore. It's about enjoying watching somebody else suffer."
Klinsmann, who is leaving Germany at the end of the season because he believes he does not fit in at Bayern, said he could understand the Dortmund player's sentiments.
"Football suffers with all these comments and arguments off the pitch," Klinsmann said. "These are things that distract people from the main point of it all which is football."
Basler, who has a reputation for speaking his mind, caused a major stir at Bayern after being substituted with Klinsmann during last weekend's match against Werder Bremen.
The talented midfielder is very annoyed that he has been been taken off so frequently this season.
"It can't go on like this," he said. "I have now been substituted in about 18 out of 20 matches. I am still going to be angry about that in 10 years."
Basler also upset his team mates by leaving the ground before the final whistle. Klinsmann is reported to have left shortly afterwards.
Bayern captain Lothar Matthaeus, known to have cool relations with Klinsmann, was quick to attack his team mates.
"If he or Basler hits two or three goals they go over to the crowd and celebrate with the fans and joke with their team mates," the former World Cup captain said.
"If they are substituted, they react as though it's an insult. That is certainly not team spirit."

The controversy could be harmful to the Bavarians since the tight Bundesliga race between Bayern, reigning champions Dortmund, Bayer Leverkusen and VfB Stuttgart is entering a decisive phase this month.
The next two weeks are especially important since Dortmund's attentions will also be fixed on European Cup semifinal clashes with Manchester United.
Bayern have a two-point lead over Leverkusen with Dortmund third a further point behind. Stuttgart are fourth, another point back.

Dortmund prepare for next week's European first leg with a difficult home game against sixth-placed Bochum on Saturday. Leverkusen travel to struggling Hansa Rostock on the same day while Stuttgart are away at bottom club Freiburg on Sunday.
